application_guidance.input_pattern: A core lower bound already exists in one of the two normalized geometries and larger dimensions are required.
read_original_when: Changing strategy domains, matrix normalization, feedback permissions or query accounting.
sensitive_conditions: Surjections must be onto to preserve both extrema.
Ball–simplex permits repeated rows and zero columns; arbitrary repeated nonzero columns need not preserve row norms or primal feasibility.
The lemma transports hardness; it does not create a hard core or prove the paper's randomized lower bound.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Exact pathwise identities; preserves the algorithm's chosen success probability rather than imposing 2/3.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: No asymptotic loss or probabilistic constants.
complexity_scope.oracle: One (A'x',A'^T y') response is simulated by one (Ax,A^T y) response; query vectors need not be strategies.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Feasible strategy pairs mapped back with equality of both full-gap expressions.
complexity_scope.resource: One joint query per joint query; public coordinate operations are free in this Oracle model.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Exact deterministic Oracle reduction, valid pathwise for arbitrary adaptive queries and randomized algorithms.

content.intended_use: Transfer game Oracle hardness from core dimensions to any coordinatewise larger dimensions.

proofs.full_local_argument: For simplex–simplex define P in {0,1}^{m×m0} by P_ia=1[rho(i)=a], and Q in {0,1}^{n×n0} by Q_jb=1[chi(j)=b]. Then A'=PAQ^T. Given arbitrary x' in R^n,y' in R^m, put x=Q^T x',y=P^T y'. One original joint query gives u=Ax,v=A^T y; return Pu,Qv. These are exactly A'x' and A'^T y'. For feasible x',y', aggregation is nonnegative and preserves total mass, hence x in Delta_n0 and y in Delta_m0. Since rho and chi are onto, max_i(PAx)_i=max_a(Ax)_a and min_j(QA^T y)_j=min_b(A^T y)_b. Both full-gap terms are preserved. All A' entries are A entries, so ||A'||max<=1. For ball–simplex use the same row incidence P and A'=[PA,0]. Write x'=(x0,xextra), and put y=P^T y'. Query A at (x0,y). Return P(Ax0) and (A^T y,0). These are the exact enlarged responses for arbitrary real inputs. Feasibility follows from ||x0||_2<=||x'||_2<=1 and from mass-preserving aggregation of y'. Surjectivity gives max_i(A'x')_i=max_a(Ax0)_a, while ||A'^T y'||_2=||(A^T y,0)||_2=||A^T y||_2. Each enlarged row is an original row followed by zeros, so its Euclidean norm is unchanged. Thus the ball–simplex full gap is equal as well. Apply these deterministic simulation and output maps after every adaptive query, keeping the same seed. Induction on the transcript yields exact simulation with one original query per enlarged query and the identical success event. This proves the hardness transfer for any specified probability requirement and preserves a query cap when one is part of the source problem.
map: Use incidence matrices of public surjections to aggregate queries and duplicate responses.
Surjectivity preserves extrema; simplex aggregation preserves feasibility.
For ball–simplex discard zero-column primal coordinates and aggregate duplicated dual coordinates; the norm term is unchanged.

assumptions: m>=m0 and n>=n0; all padding maps and coordinate ordering are public and fixed independently of the unknown matrix entries.
For simplex–simplex choose surjections rho:[m]->[m0] and chi:[n]->[n0], and set A'_ij=A_rho(i),chi(j).
For ball–simplex choose a row surjection rho:[m]->[m0], duplicate rows to form Atilde, and set A'=[Atilde,0] with n−n0 zero columns.
statement.conclusion: A' remains admissible. Each enlarged query is exactly simulated with one joint query to A. Aggregation maps enlarged feasible strategies to original feasible strategies with exactly equal full gaps. Therefore any lower bound for an original core instance transfers to the corresponding enlarged instance without query, error or probability loss.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let A be a real m0×n0 matrix, with positive integer m0,n0. Delta_k={z>=0:1^T z=1}, B_2^k={z:||z||_2<=1}. For simplex–simplex, X=Delta_n0,Y=Delta_m0, ||A||max<=1 and Gap_A(x,y)=max_i(Ax)_i−min_j(A^T y)_j. For ball–simplex, X=B_2^n0,Y=Delta_m0, max_i||A_i,:||_2<=1 and Gap_A(x,y)=max_i(Ax)_i+||A^T y||_2. A joint query returns (Ax,A^T y) on arbitrary real vectors.
statement.parameter_domains: Positive integers m0,n0,m,n with m>=m0,n>=n0; either of the two specified geometries separately; any target gap accuracy.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible A, every enlarged real joint query and every feasible enlarged output, the following identities hold deterministically. Consequently any deterministic or randomized adaptive algorithm for A' can be simulated on A with the same private randomness and success event, at one original joint query per enlarged joint query. The lemma imposes no particular probability threshold or intrinsic query cap.

summary: Public surjections duplicate simplex rows/columns; ball–simplex duplicates rows and adds zero columns. Every enlarged joint query costs one original joint query, and feasible outputs preserve the full gap exactly.
title: Exact gap-preserving dimension extension for two matrix-game geometries
use_when: Extend an established lower bound to larger dimensions of the same normalized geometry without changing accuracy or success probability.
